issue_context.title: Async context is broken for POST requests when its created inside 'onRequest' hook
comments:
This has nothing to do with nest 🤷 

edit: I haven't cleaned up the repro fully (e.g. project name and NPM scripts), but there is no nestjs involved in it

This is actually a nice bug report, thanks. I'll try to take a look as it seems quite serious.

Have you tried just using an onRequest hook to set the ALS? This should not be related at all with middie.

Nope, tbh this is the very first time me using fastify directly :] Can this be done via hooks? I need to use `storage.run` with a callback where the context will work, so I need to wrap the request handler, with hooks I could only attach something to the request object, no?

Agreed this is quite serious, at least for MikroORM users.

@B4nan fairly sure it's the same thing as https://github.com/fastify/fastify-request-context/pull/12, see also issue linked in it.
fastify-request-context is recommended way to handle async contexts in fastify, it solves this issue entirely.

> Could you please try to substitute your first fastify.use with this, and see if it solves the problem?

`enterWith` helps, but it is not actual solution. it will keep the async context open. imagine there is a handler where we want the context, and another one where we do not want the context. with `enterWith`, we would keep the async context created by first handler also for the other one. we need boundaries for this.
Here is the Node core issue about this: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/41285.
Thanks a lot for additional debugging and escalating this!

> > Could you please try to substitute your first fastify.use with this, and see if it solves the problem?
> 
> `enterWith` helps, but it is not actual solution. it will keep the async context open. imagine there is a handler where we want the context, and another one where we do not want the context. with `enterWith`, we would keep the async context created by first handler also for the other one. we need boundaries for this.

If you need to handle the lifetime of your async context you can extend the [`AsyncResource`](https://nodejs.org/api/async_context.html#class-asyncresource) class and `bind` your storage functions. Hope this helps
